title: Multi-Obligation Invariants — joint-context binding, temporal logic, six categories; 'green nodes do not automatically create a green system'

source.source_reference: Shawn's explicit teaching, main chat, 2026-10-10. Filed same-evening per his standing law: his word IS the verification (Verification Law); filed immediately, not queued.

intelligence.essence: Invariants that hold across several obligations at once — the rules the whole system must never break. Joint-context binding (the D-101/D-102 case: two obligations joined on a key must actually share the key's meaning, not just its spelling) prevents the classic join fallacy. Temporal logic governs invariants over time: what must hold always, eventually, or until. Six categories cover the invariant space. Race handling (T1–T4) covers multi-party timing. The governing image, from Shawn's own diagram: green nodes do not automatically create a green system — every node can pass and the composition can still violate the invariant, because the invariant is about the whole, not the parts.

human_view.meaning: Some rules are about the whole system, not any single part. 'Every part is fine' doesn't prove 'the whole is fine' — the rule about the whole needs its own check. And when two parts join on the same key, make sure they mean the same thing by it, not just spell it the same.
human_view.why_it_matters: The composition fallacy, killed as law. This is the formal version of the intuition in Shawn's own diagram.
